blocks.text: Ostrevia 10 mg film-coated tablets
Ostrevia 25 mg film-coated tablets
Each film-coated tablet contains 10 mg or 25 mg lumiravostat.
Excipient with known effect: each tablet contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg), that is to say essentially "sodium-free". For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.
Film-coated tablet.
10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "10" on the other.
25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "25" on the other.
Ostrevia is indicated for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema that has not responded adequately to potent topical corticosteroids, or when these are not advisable.
The recommended dose is 10 mg once daily, with or without food. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily if the response is inadequate after 12 weeks.
Moderate hepatic impairment: 10 mg once daily. Severe hepatic impairment: not recommended.
With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ketoconazole or clarithromycin): 10 mg once daily.
Method of administration: oral use. Swallow the tablet whole with water.
Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. Active tuberculosis or active serious infection. Pregnancy (see section 4.6).

subs.title: Special warnings and precautions for use

blocks.text: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported, some leading to hospitalization or death. Screen patients for latent tuberculosis before starting treatment and treat it first. Interrupt treatment if a serious infection develops.
Malignancy, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, has been reported. Consider the risks and benefits before starting treatment in patients with a known malignancy.
Venous thromboembolism, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has been reported. Use with caution in patients with risk factors and stop treatment if it occurs.
Monitor lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months.

subs.title: Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction

blocks.text: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase lumiravostat exposure (use 10 mg once daily). Strong CYP3A4 inducers, such as rifampicin, reduce exposure; avoid concomitant use.

Lumiravostat caused embryo-fetal toxicity in rats and rabbits. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
It is not known whether lumiravostat passes into human milk. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose.

subs.title: Effects on ability to drive and use machines

blocks.text: Ostrevia has no or negligible influence on the ability to drive and use machines.

It allows continued monitoring of the benefit/risk balance of the medicinal product. Healthcare professionals are asked to report any suspected adverse reactions via the Yellow Card Scheme at www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard or search for MHRA Yellow Card in the Google Play or Apple App Store.
There is no specific antidote. Monitor the patient for signs of adverse reactions and give supportive treatment. Lumiravostat is not removed by haemodialysis to a meaningful extent.
Lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase, which signals downstream of several cytokines involved in skin inflammation.
Dose-dependent reductions in markers of skin inflammation were seen within 2 weeks.

Clinical efficacy: In two 16-week placebo-controlled studies (fictional HANDS-1 and HANDS-2, 1,210 adults), 38% of patients on lumiravostat 25 mg and 31% on 10 mg reached clear or almost clear hands, against 12% on placebo.
Peak plasma concentrations are reached 1 to 2 hours after a dose. The half-life is about 16 hours. Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.
Lumiravostat was not genotoxic. Embryo-fetal toxicity was seen in rats and rabbits at exposures close to the human exposure at 25 mg.
Microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow).

sections.title: 1. What Ostrevia is and what it is used for

blocks.text: Ostrevia contains the active substance lumiravostat. It calms the immune activity that causes long-lasting hand eczema. It is used in adults when creams with strong corticosteroids have not helped enough or cannot be used.

sections.title: 2. What you need to know before you take Ostrevia

items: if you are allergic to lumiravostat or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section 6)
if you have tuberculosis or another serious infection

blocks.text: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Ostrevia if you have an infection, have had cancer, or have had blood clots. Your doctor will test you for tuberculosis and do blood tests before and during treatment.
Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking, have recently taken or might take any other medicines, especially ketoconazole, clarithromycin or rifampicin.
Do not take Ostrevia if you are pregnant. Use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after your last dose. Do not breast-feed during treatment and for 4 days after your last dose.
Ostrevia is not expected to affect your ability to drive or use machines.
Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. The usual dose is one 10 mg tablet once a day. Your doctor may increase it to 25 mg once a day.

subs.title: If you take more Ostrevia than you should

blocks.text: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist straight away.

subs.title: If you forget to take Ostrevia

blocks.text: Take it as soon as you remember on the same day. Do not take a double dose to make up for a forgotten tablet.
Talk to your doctor before you stop.

Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them. Tell your doctor straight away if you get signs of a serious infection (fever, cough, painful skin rash) or of a blood clot (painful swollen leg, chest pain, sudden breathlessness).

Very common (may affect more than 1 in 10 people): cold symptoms. Common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people): headache, nausea, acne, shingles, changes in blood tests. Uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people): pneumonia, skin infection, blood clots.

If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the Yellow Card Scheme at www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard or search for MHRA Yellow Card in the Google Play or Apple App Store. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.

Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children. Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the carton and blister after EXP. Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use.
